title: Regression tests in CI
subtitle: Every PR that touches the assistant runs the set and can turn red
mission: At Aurora, anyone on the team opens PRs on the assistant: prompt, model, chunk size. Now every PR runs set 2026-10 (60 questions, 20 of them critical: outside the handbook or delicate) on GitHub Actions, and the gate decides whether it can be merged. Tune the gate to block what gets worse and let through what gets better.

why.simples:
Before serving a new dish, the kitchen tastes it. If the recipe changed (less salt, another supplier), it tastes again, always the same way. And some things must never happen, like peanuts in the dish of someone allergic: then it doesn’t matter how good the rest is.
CI is that automatic tasting: every change to the assistant runs the same questions, and the merge only happens if the score doesn’t drop and no critical case fails.
why.dev:
The gate has three rules, each catching a kind of regression: an absolute minimum score (the cheaper model drops to 77%), a maximum drop against main (the baseline stored at the last merge) and critical cases that block on their own, outside the average (refusing what isn’t in the handbook, handing harassment to a person). The script exits non-zero when any fails, and GitHub Actions marks the job as failed; with a branch protection rule requiring that job, the merge is blocked.
Run the eval only when what affects answers changes (paths filter), pin the model version, keep the log of flipped cases and update baseline.json only after merging. LLM evaluation varies a little between runs: leave a few points of slack in the max drop and, for critical cases, run more than once before blaming the PR.
why.especialista:
Regressions also arrive without a PR. In January 2024, UK delivery firm DPD’s support chatbot swore at a customer and wrote a poem criticizing the company; DPD blamed an error after a system update and switched the AI part off. A provider model change, an index change or a dependency bump is a production change: run the same gate on a schedule (daily, say) and on every version bump, not only on PRs.
Cost matters: 60 questions with an LLM judge per PR is cheap; 5,000 isn’t. Keep a fast smoke set for every PR and the full one for merges to main or nightly. And remember the gate only catches what the set contains: a critical case nobody wrote blocks nothing (next lessons: hard cases and user feedback).

steps:
In the assistant’s repository (with assistant.py from the Practice mission and evals/rh/2026-10.jsonl from lesson 1), create gate.py. It runs the set, compares with main’s baseline and exits with an error if the score falls below the minimum, drops more than 3 points or any critical case (kind outside or sensitive) fails:
import json
import pathlib
import sys

from assistant import handle

SET = pathlib.Path("evals/rh/2026-10.jsonl")
MIN_SCORE = float(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 0.80
MAX_DROP = 0.03
EXPECTED = {"answer": "answer", "outside": "refuse", "sensitive": "handoff"}

cases = [json.loads(line) for line in SET.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines() if line.strip()]
BASELINE = pathlib.Path("evals/rh/baseline.json")
baseline = json.loads(BASELINE.read_text()) if BASELINE.exists() else {"score": 0.0}

fails = []
critical_fails = []
for case in cases:
    r = handle(case["question"])
    ok = r["action"] == EXPECTED[case["kind"]]
    if ok and case["kind"] == "answer":
        ok = bool(set(r["cited"]) & set(case["gold"]))
    if not ok:
        fails.append(case["id"])
        if case["kind"] != "answer":
            critical_fails.append(case["id"])

score = 1 - len(fails) / len(cases)
print(f"score {score:.0%} (main {baseline['score']:.0%}) | failed: {fails}")

problems = []
if score < MIN_SCORE:
    problems.append(f"score below {MIN_SCORE:.0%}")
if baseline["score"] - score > MAX_DROP:
    problems.append(f"dropped more than {MAX_DROP:.0%} vs main")
if critical_fails:
    problems.append(f"critical cases failed: {critical_fails}")

if problems:
    sys.exit("FAILED: " + "; ".join(problems))
print("PASSED")

Run it on main (without baseline.json the drop isn’t checked) and store the baseline, replacing 0.85 with the score you got:
python gate.py 0.0
echo '{"score": 0.85}' > evals/rh/baseline.json

Create .github/workflows/eval-rh.yml. It runs on every PR that touches the assistant, the corpus or the set:
name: eval-rh

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - "assistant.py"
      - "corpus.py"
      - "evals/**"

jobs:
  eval:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
      - run: pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu
      - run: pip install sentence-transformers rank_bm25 anthropic
      - run: python gate.py 0.80
        env:
          ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}

Store the key in Settings > Secrets and variables > Actions as ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (PRs from forks don’t get secrets). In Settings > Branches, add a protection rule for main requiring the "eval" check. Then open a PR that deletes the refusal sentence from SYSTEM.
recipe.ok: the PR’s eval job turns red with "FAILED: critical cases failed: [...]" and the merge button is blocked; when you undo the change, the job turns green with PASSED.
